subject: Re: Margin guard schedule — amendment punchlist and redlines
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@lumenhealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@lumenhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-03T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Margin guard schedule — initial redlines

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for walking through the Order Form earlier. Our legal and procurement teams reviewed the pricing exhibit and flagged a few fixes we need before we can move to counter-signature. High level items: 

1) "Price envelope" calculation allows a negative carry that would let Redwood clawback credits post-true-up — LumenHealth needs an express floor that prevents any retroactive debit beyond the paid amount.
2) The tiered packaging language references "SKU equivalence" but does not define how bundled SKUs are mapped during a downturn — we need a mapping table or an explicit parity clause.
3) Stabilization/holdback mechanics: the draft allows Redwood to apply a stabilization surcharge with 30 days' notice; LH needs either a longer notice window (60 days) or a cap on the incremental surcharge.
4) Clarify that any usage-based surcharges will be applied on an annual true-up basis and cannot be levied intra-year without mutual written consent.

I attached our annotated redlines (Attachment: LumenHealth_Redlines_v4.pdf). Please provide a short punchlist of proposed language changes and, if possible, a clean Order Form that incorporates the agreed mechanics for the margin/holdback so our procurement team can circulate internally.

Would appreciate a response by COB Monday so we can keep the timeline for 11/15 signature.

Best,
Aisha Khan
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Procurement
LumenHealth

Attachment: LumenHealth_Redlines_v4.pdf (PDF, 256 KB)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Margin guard schedule — initial redlines

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines.

High level response up front: we are open to a negotiated floor that prevents a post-true-up debit beyond prior paid amounts, and we can provide a SKU-bundling parity table for the Order Form. The stabilization notice period is something we can flex (we typically run 30 days but see why 60 matters for you).

I've attached a short matrix mapping how the margin guard calculation would behave under three scenarios (growth, neutral, decline) and a proposed revision to the stabilization clause. That matrix includes the explicit "no-retro-debit" floor language we think would address your #1. Please review the spreadsheet and let us know whether the math and the examples map to your procurement team's expectations.

I'll have Marissa (legal) weigh in on the final clause language; Karthik is on the thread for packaging/SKU technical mapping questions.

Grace O'Connor
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RW-Response_Margin_Guard_Matrix.xlsx (Excel, 48 KB)

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@lumenhealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@lumenhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-04T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Margin guard schedule — initial redlines

Thanks Grace — we reviewed the matrix this morning. A few comments inline: 

- The "no-retro-debit" floor example looks promising, but the spreadsheet ties the floor to an accounting definition that does not match LH policy. We need the floor to be explicitly pegged to "annual invoiced amount for the affected SKU family" (not to the model in your sample).
- For SKU mapping: the example bundles map cleanly when usage drops under 15%, but we need a deterministic tie-breaker for partial bundles (e.g., when one SKU declines 10% and its paired SKU declines 25%). The tie-breaker must be spelled out.
- Stabilization cap: LH legal will accept a 60-day notice window only if the incremental surcharge is capped at 12% in any rolling 12-month window. 

I'll mark up the matrix and return with a suggested tie-breaker text. For timing: if Redwood can accept the 60-day notice + 12% cap + invoice-pegged floor, we can proceed to finalize.

Aisha

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@lumenhealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Margin guard schedule — initial redlines (Redwood legal input)

Aisha / Grace — looping in brief legal commentary and a proposed compromise.

1) Floor language: proposed sentence to add to Exhibit B — "Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary, under no circumstances shall Redwood seek to debit LumenHealth for amounts in excess of the cumulative invoiced charges for the applicable SKU family during the corresponding annual billing period (the \"Invoice Floor\")." This is narrow and maps to your ask to peg the floor to invoiced amounts.

2) Tie-breaker for partial bundles: propose a deterministic allocation: "If SKU bundle components diverge, the bundle shall be reallocated pro rata based on the prior 3-month rolling usage for each component; where rounding ambiguity exists, the higher-frequency SKU shall be prioritized." This avoids subjective negotiations while protecting both parties.

3) Stabilization cap and notice: Redwood accepts 60 days' notice and will commit to a 12% cap in any rolling 12-month window on incremental stabilization surcharges. We will also add a cross-check requiring Redwood to provide simulated billing impact and a short remediation plan when stabilization is triggered.

If those three items are acceptable, I can incorporate the exact tracked language into OrderForm_v3 and return a clean PDF for signature.

Marissa Cole
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Internal_Legal_Notes.txt (plain text, 3 KB)

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@lumenhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@lumenhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-06T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Margin guard schedule — initial redlines

Marissa/Grace — this reads clean and addresses our concerns with two small exceptions: 

• The pro rata reallocation should use the prior 6-month rolling usage (not 3-month) to smooth seasonality effects.
• The Invoice Floor should explicitly survive termination for the accounting period in which it was accrued (so we don't see clawbacks in post-termination reconciliations).

If Redwood agrees to those two tweaks (6-month rolling window; Invoice Floor survives termination for that annual billing period), LH can approve and circulate for signature tomorrow.

Aisha

Attachment: LumenHealth_FinalChecklist.txt (plain text, 1 KB)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-07T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Final — Margin guard schedule amendments and next steps

Aisha — thanks, and appreciate the quick turnaround. Redwood accepts the two final tweaks: 

• Change pro rata allocation to a prior 6-month rolling usage window.
• Add survival language for the Invoice Floor such that it survives termination for reconciliation of the applicable annual billing period.

Marissa has incorporated those edits into OrderForm_v3-annotated.pdf (attached). We will also append the stabilization simulation template to the Order Form as an annex for transparency when a stabilization action is proposed.

Next steps: 
• Please confirm acceptance on this email thread and procurement will route for signature.
• Once you confirm, we will push the annotated Order Form into DocuSign (I included the link in the related_links field).

Thanks and looking forward to closing this week.

Grace O'Connor
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: OrderForm_v3-annotated.pdf (PDF, 92 KB); Stabilization_Simulation_Template.csv (CSV, 12 KB)
